historical_references.reference: Rasteen was an important basin city in the Sassanid Empire, located at the juncture of the Karun and Karkheh rivers. It was a major center for agriculture and trade, and was renowned for its silk production.

After the Islamic conquest of Persia, Rasteen became an important Islamic city and remained a significant cultural and economic center. It was a major stop on the Silk Road, and its mosques and madrasas attracted scholars from around the Muslim world.
